sources.entry: cxpak by Barnett Studios - A code-intelligence Claude Code plugin and MCP server (Rust, single binary, 43 languages) that builds a typed dependency graph and packs token-budgeted, annotated context bundles for any task. Exceptionally engineered and security-forward — 2,400+ tests, recorded ADRs, a sandboxed WASM plugin SDK, and cosign-signed, SBOM-attested release images.

summary.one_liner: cxpak is a Rust code-intelligence tool and MCP server that indexes a codebase with tree-sitter, builds a typed dependency graph, and packs token-budgeted context bundles for LLMs and Claude Code.
summary.what_it_does: cxpak parses source with tree-sitter across 44 languages and builds a typed dependency graph that includes schema, migration, and embedded-SQL links. It produces token-budgeted context bundles for a given task, with per-file annotations explaining why each file was included, and a Repo-DNA convention summary at the start of each response. It offers intelligence reports such as health score, risk ranking, architecture coupling, blast radius, dead code, call graph, security surface, and data flow. It exposes these through a CLI, an MCP server (five intent-parameterized tools), an HTTP server, and an LSP server. It also renders a self-contained offline HTML dashboard and graph views, with export to Mermaid, SVG, PNG, C4, JSON, Cypher, and GraphML.
use_cases: give an LLM focused context for a coding task
trace a symbol through a codebase's dependencies
assess change impact before editing code
onboard onto an unfamiliar repository with a reading order
review changes against observed code conventions
how_to_run: brew tap Barnett-Studios/tap && brew install cxpak
notable: Serves an MCP server with five intent-parameterized tools, with a shared background index server on macOS/Linux
Ranks context with six deterministic signals fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion; embeddings are an optional opt-in seventh signal
Visual dashboard is a single self-contained HTML file with inlined D3 and no external assets
Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in docs/adrs/
Live Postgres/MySQL schema introspection is read-only and off by default behind a build feature
caveats: The WASM plugin system is a skeleton: no plugin code can run yet, and the plugins feature is excluded from default builds
Live database introspection requires the data-introspect build feature and is off by default
The README says the project is under development and the surface still moves
Shared index server is macOS/Linux only; Windows always indexes in-process
